Blueface, whose real name is Johnathan Jamall Porter, is an American rapper, songwriter, entertainer, and social media personality from Los Angeles, California. Born on January 20, 1997, Blueface rose to fame in 2018 and became widely recognized for his unique offbeat rapping style, viral personality, and unpredictable antics on social media.

Blueface grew up in Los Angeles, California, and attended Arleta High School, where he played quarterback for the school’s football team. Before pursuing music full-time, he briefly attended Fayetteville State University in North Carolina.

He began releasing music in 2017 and gained national attention in 2018 after his song “Respect My Cryppin’” went viral. His unconventional flow, distinctive voice, and charismatic personality quickly separated him from other emerging West Coast rappers.

His biggest breakthrough came with the release of “Thotiana,” which became a massive hit in 2019, reaching No. 8 on the Billboard Hot 100. The song received popular remixes featuring Cardi B and YG, helping Blueface establish himself in mainstream hip-hop.

Throughout his career, Blueface has collaborated with artists including Lil Baby, Offset, NLE Choppa, and other major names in the music industry.
